topics.label: Introduction and overview of cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by introducing the learning outcomes and the conceptual model of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signaling pathways and oncogenic mutations in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in receptor pathways like Wnt and receptor tyrosine kinase cascades drive sustained proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation block in hematological and epithelial cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how arrested differentiation maintains cells in proliferative progenitor states in both leukemias and intestinal carcinomas.

topics.label: Mechanisms of apoptotic resistance in cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how cancer cells evade programmed cell death through mutations in p53 and altered balances of Bcl-2 family proteins.

topics.label: Telomere biology, senescence bypass, and p53 stress responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how telomere shortening triggers senescence, how cancer cells achieve replicative immortality through telomerase reactivation, and how p53 mediates stress-induced growth arrest.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in tumor biology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how cancer cells rewire metabolic pathways through aerobic glycolysis and Krebs cycle mutations to support growth and alter the epigenome.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis and vascular recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how tumors overcome hypoxia and nutrient deprivation by shifting the balance of signaling factors to stimulate new blood vessel growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and genomics of cancer metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the multi-step metastatic cascade, circulating tumor cell monitoring, microenvironmental compatibility, and the genomic features of metastatic clones.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by summarising the integration of hallmarks in cancer biology and outlining upcoming practical sessions.
